name: Eosinophilic Gastroenteritis

criteria.description: GI symptoms (abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, bloating, weight loss)
Eosinophilic infiltration of one or more areas of the GI tract on biopsy (>= 20 eos/hpf in stomach; >= 20 eos/hpf in small bowel)
Exclusion of other causes of tissue eosinophilia (parasites, IBD, malignancy, hypereosinophilic syndrome, drug reaction)
Personal or family history of atopy/allergic disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: GI symptoms with histological demonstration of eosinophilic infiltration of the GI tract (stomach and/or intestine) after exclusion of other causes of eosinophilia.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Three subtypes based on layer involved: mucosal (most common), muscular (obstruction), and serosal (ascites). Serosal form often has eosinophilic ascites.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal pain with peripheral eosinophilia and GI eosinophilic infiltration
pathognomonic.notes: The combination is highly characteristic but not pathognomonic alone

rare.notes: Ascitic fluid rich in eosinophils; serosal subtype
From eosinophilic infiltration of muscularis causing thickening and stenosis

laboratory: Iron deficiency anemia (if mucosal involvement with bleeding)
imaging: CT abdomen: thickened gastric/bowel wall, ascites (serosal type), possible obstruction
CT enterography: mucosal enhancement, fold thickening, luminal narrowing
Small bowel follow-through: thickened folds, nodularity, narrowing
genetic: Eotaxin (CCL11, CCL24, CCL26) polymorphisms implicated in susceptibility
other: Upper endoscopy/colonoscopy with biopsies: mucosal erythema, nodularity, ulceration
Multiple biopsies from affected areas needed (patchy distribution)
Eosinophilic ascites: paracentesis shows > 500 eosinophils/microL (serosal type)
Full-thickness biopsy may be needed for muscular/serosal subtypes

distinguishingFeatures: EoE is limited to the esophagus
EoE presents primarily with dysphagia and food impaction
HES has persistent eosinophilia > 1500/microL for > 6 months
HES involves multiple organs (cardiac, pulmonary, dermatologic) beyond GI
Parasitic infections confirmed by stool ova/parasite or serology

redFlags: Massive ascites with respiratory compromise (serosal subtype)
Persistent eosinophilia > 1500 with multi-organ involvement (rule out HES)
references: Talley NJ, et al. Eosinophilic gastroenteritis: a clinicopathological study of patients with disease of the mucosa, muscle layer, and subserosal tissues. Gut. 1990;31(1):54-58.
Zhang L, et al. Eosinophilic gastroenteritis: clinical profiles and therapeutic outcomes. BMC Gastroenterol. 2014;14:14.
Pineton de Chambrun G, et al. Eosinophilic gastroenteritis. Clin Res Hepatol Gastroenterol. 2011;35(4):253-256.
